thesis: The bear carries present-entry caution because broad revenue growth does not establish normalised owner-cash value at the snapshot premium. The bull establishes operating quality after separating refunds, preventing a deterioration-based sell ruling. A simple $1.91 quarterly EPS adjustment is not a complete normalised growth comparison.
strongest_counterexample: Revenue grew 16% across products and geographies with record quarterly CFO; tariff refunds do not account for this broad demand expansion.
invalidation_conditions: A complete comparable earnings/cash bridge excluding the $0.11 EPS and approximately two-point gross-margin refund effects shows positive normalised earnings growth and positive cash after capex/debt service, resolving the key operating-to-owner-cash gap.
A subsequent comparable revenue growth rate at or below zero would invalidate the retained broad-demand expansion premise.
evidence_gaps: Debt, post-capex cash and owner-cash yield.
Matched valuation and persistence of product/geographic growth.
decisive_factors: 38.17x vendor reference lacks normalised fair-value support.
Tariff effects inflate headline EPS and gross margin.
Slowing MACD and weak volume show consolidation rather than fresh entry confirmation.
